newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee in crisis says industry chief.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee in crisis says industry chief.

text.p: Colombia's coffee industry is reaching crisis point and may soon no longer be viable, the head of the National Coffee Growers' Federation said.

The comments by Jorge Cardenas coincided with a televised speech Monday night by President Ernesto Samper in which he criticized the central bank for standing idle while the peso strengthened against the dollar, slashing the peso value of export earnings and forcing up consumer prices.
"The coffee industry is coming to the point of no return where it will no longer be viable," Cardenas said at a weekly meeting of the federation.

The dollar has been sliding steadily against the dollar of late and is now at its weakest since early January. The peso was officially projected to lose 13.6 percent in 1996 but so far this year has lost less than 3 percent against the dollar.

In his weekly address to the nation, Samper chided the central bank's exchange rate policy, saying: "The tactic used by the central bank is just to watch the peso revalue...we will pressure the central bank to contribute its share and stop this perverse taxi meter of the peso revaluation."

Coupled with inflation running at 18.4 percent for the year to date -- well above the central bank's target of 17 percent for the entire year -- coffee growers have seen production costs forced up and potential export earnings decline.

The National Coffee Fund, which is operated by the coffee federation and purchases the crop from growers, is predicted to post a 120 billion peso deficit for the 1995-96 coffee year. That figure may rise to 180 billion pesos by the end of the new year which began last week.
The peso closed at 1,009.25 per dollar Monday, its strongest since January 12.
